story: Friday evening at Sumter Oaks has Gary and Donna at pickleball court one in the Rec Center, where Donna is counting out loud as Gary works through ten third-shot drops at the kitchen line. Hal has settled in nearby to watch a few points and keep an eye on the clock, with a possible turn on court two if his knee cooperates. Meanwhile, Rosa has left her house and is heading out along Magnolia Loop in the breezy, 76-degree October air.
events: Gary (pickleball court 1): Pick up my paddle and work on third-shot drop drills with Donna
Rosa headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).

gary.thought_process: Hal just said his piece about the cart and the clipboard, and I already answered him a tick ago, so no need to rehash it. Donna and I have court one for two hours and I promised to keep to that limit. The third-shot drops are the best part of my week, and the parade is tomorrow, so I should enjoy this hour. The cart stays in the garage until the committee signs off, and I'm glad Hal is easy about it. Best move is to get on with the drills.

parameters.content: Pick up my paddle and work on third-shot drop drills with Donna

donna.thought_process: Gary and I have court one for two hours, and Hal just wandered in and offered to watch. Gary has already covered the court two offer. Rather than repeat the invite, I should get the practice moving: the ladder match is coming and Gary's third-shot drops are the weak spot. I'll hand Gary a clear drill instruction, keep it upbeat, and let Hal watch if he likes. Also a nice moment to remind Hal the cart's headed to Architectural Review properly.

parameters.content: Okay, Gary, enough chatting, grab your paddle and get to the kitchen line. Soft hands on the third shot, ten drops in a row, and I'm counting out loud.

hal.thought_process: Gary and Donna both spoke to me last tick, and Gary offered court two after their game. I've already told Gary the cart's fine and I'm keeping the clipboard in the drawer. No need to nag again. Donna asked me to watch Gary's third-shot drops, so I'll do that, answer her plainly, and be neighborly for once. The flamingo count can wait until after the parade.

parameters.content: I'll watch a few points, Donna. Two hours on court one, I see the board says so, and I'll hold Gary to the clock. Court two after, maybe, if my knee cooperates.

rosa.thought_process: I've got the treats by the door, the shift schedule is clear, the counters are wiped, and the coffee is done. The plan for tomorrow is set: Gary and Donna meet me at the Loop for the parade cart. No one is nearby to talk to, and sitting here any longer won't help. Magnolia Loop is the only place to go, and I can check on the cart setup and the neighborhood's Halloween mood before tomorrow's crowd arrives. Better to walk over now while the weather is nice and see who's out.

parameters.content: Heading out to the Loop to check on the parade cart setup and see who's around before tomorrow.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
